$comment: The shared WE-4 / AT-1 attestation-nonce type corpus. THREE CONSUMERS, ONE FILE: tools/check-nonce-type.py runs it against the Python reference AND against spec/schemas/wire/attestation_object.schema.json's pattern, and crates/acp-decision/tests/quorum.rs runs it against the Rust check. It exists because those definitions DID diverge and nothing caught it -- the schema pinned {22}== from its first day, the reference accepted any length, and no fixture ever fed a wrong-length nonce, so both stayed green for a release. Aligning them by hand once was never the fix; this is. A null `clause` means the value conforms. Otherwise it is the refusal NAME, and the name is asserted rather than merely the fact of a refusal, because a check that refuses under the wrong clause has told the reader something false.

cases.why: the conforming form: b64: + RFC 4648 sec 4 base64 with padding, 128-bit. The seed is chosen so this value contains BOTH + and /, or the url-safe case below would differ from it in nothing
all-zero bytes are a legal nonce; the type says nothing about entropy
ACP-87: the prefix stripped. Two ids for one object, two ledger slots
padding omitted. WE-4 says reject rather than normalize
RFC 4648 sec 5 alphabet. Same length, same decoded bytes, DIFFERENT STRING -- the only shape AT-1 cannot also catch, which is why the WE-4 mutant is paired with it and not with the unprefixed case
one character is never base64; the pre-ACP-88 pattern accepted it
three characters unpadded; the pre-ACP-88 pattern accepted it
five characters: not a whole number of four-character groups
the unanchored-pattern bait. A partial match here is the defect itself, not a check against it
padding inside the body rather than only at its end
four padding characters; at most two are legal
the empty string carries no type at all
well-formed and empty: WE-4 is satisfied and AT-1 is not. The two clause names differ here, which is the whole reason the rules are split
64-bit. Exactly what WE-4 demands; half of what AT-1 requires. A 2^-32 birthday collision is ONE id for TWO attestations -- Z4 from the other side
256-bit. Over-long is refused too: AT-1 states a size, not a minimum
